issues.failure_explanation: The formula asserts that uniqueness of the rank-r decomposition of T^(f) fails at r = n_codim^f + 1 for every f other than a Segre-type f with two entries equal to 1 and a factor of dimension 2. But at r = n_codim^f + 1 a general (r-1)-plane spanned by r general points of X meets X in exactly deg X points (Bezout, transverse for a general configuration), so uniqueness also holds whenever deg X = n_codim^f + 1, i.e., whenever the Segre-Veronese X is of minimal degree. This includes rational normal curves (ell=1, m_1=2, any f_1>=2), the Veronese surface (ell=1, f_1=2, m_1=3), the scrolls nu_(1,k)(P^1 x P^1), and linear X. Concrete counterexample: ell=1, d=3, m_1=2, f=(2): the column space is spanned by v_1^{⊗2}, v_2^{⊗2}; the secant line to the conic nu_2(P^1) meets it in exactly these 2 points, so the rank-2 decomposition is unique and r(f)=2 (=n_col), while the formula gives min{2,1}=1. The proof's assertion 'For all other tuples f, we have deg X > r' is false (for the conic, deg X = 2 = r at the boundary).

issues.failure_explanation: Multiplying the eigenvector equations (eq:vw) by v^H and w^H yields lambda*||v||^2 = beta_1 + mu/alpha_1 and lambda*||w||^2 = (lambda/alpha_2)mu_bar + beta_2, since the eigenvector pair is normalized (||v||^2 + ||w||^2 = 1, as the proof itself uses), not ||v|| = ||w|| = 1. issues.title: Eigenvalue equations in the local-convergence proof drop norm factors
issues.why_classification: The repair is routine algebra within the existing proof plus a standard local nondegeneracy condition; the stated conclusion survives for the intended (generic) critical points.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem assumes only genericity and dim A = r, with no rank bound, but uniqueness of the rank-one left singular vector requires that the only rank-one elements of A (the span of the full rank-one tensors R^(i)_(d)) are the R^(i)_(d) themselves. Counterexample: ell = 1, d = 3, f = 1, m_1 = 2, r = 4: four general v_i^{⊗3} span S^3(R^2), so M_A is orthogonal and M M^T = I_3; every unit vector in S^2(R^2) -- in particular every rank-one w⊗w with w != ±v_i -- is a left singular vector of M with singular value 1, contradicting uniqueness. The proof invokes 'r <= r(f)', which is neither a hypothesis nor the right quantity (r(f) governs the f-flattening's column space, not the full span; the needed hypothesis is that the only rank-one elements of A are the generators, e.g. r <= n_codim^d), and the sentence asserting that the R^(i)_(f) are 'the only rank-one elements in A' is type-inconsistent (they are not elements of A). Moreover, the theorem concerns the full-span stacked tensor, which the algorithm never computes (Algorithm 2 reconstructs complements from the row span of T^(f)), so it does not justify the cited reconstruction step.

issues.failure_explanation: The loop's core step presumes that Algorithm 1 (PS-HOPM) returns a pSVT with singular value one. The paper's own convergence theorem guarantees only convergence to some pSVT (an arbitrary first-order critical point), and the paper explicitly notes that PS-HOPM may converge to critical points that are not globally optimal -- the sigma = 1 pSVTs are the global maximizers of F_A. The algorithm contains no verification or restart mechanism ensuring sigma = 1, so the specified steps can return a non-component pSVT, after which the completion and deflation steps corrupt the output. The stated output (the full decomposition) is therefore not delivered by the procedure as written, and the abstract's claim of 'correctness of the algorithm' holds only conditionally on this unguaranteed step.
